key_insight: A sparse, calibrated regularized-Stokeslet force model can reproduce the dominant near-field flow of a swimming bacterium in both free space and near a wall while using far fewer force points than a high-fidelity model.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the cost and memory of velocity-field evaluation, making large-scale simulations of multi-swimmer hydrodynamics more practical without losing key near-field physics.
method: Calibrate sparse force locations/strengths by constrained least-squares fitting to a high-fidelity single-bacterium velocity field.
Enforce force-free and torque-free swimming constraints to preserve self-propulsion physics.
Use PCA to compress phase-dependent force variation and fit modal coefficients as continuous functions of flagellar phase.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the reduced-order model preserves dominant reference-flow structures in both free space and near a no-slip boundary, with wall-induced redirection captured and residual error mainly concentrated near the cell body.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the calibration quality and the chosen regularization parameter, and the remaining discrepancy is largest near the cell body, especially in near-wall cases.
paper_title: A Calibrated Reduced-Order Force Model for Bacterial Hydrodynamics in Free Space and Near a Planar Boundary
